messages:
zoe: ran into a confusing one in the onboarding sample: req-id present on initial send but missing on retry and span still links correctly. repo: https://git.internal/samples/telemetry-backoff :wave:

zoe: minimal logs (node sample, default env):

```
INFO 2026-04-05T08:12:01Z outgoing.request method=POST path=/api/generate headers={"x-request-id":"rid-2f9"}
WARN 2026-04-05T08:12:01Z upstream returned 503 will retry
DEBUG 2026-04-05T08:12:01Z retry building new request attempt=1
INFO 2026-04-05T08:12:01Z outgoing.request method=POST path=/api/generate headers={}
```

zoe: OTEL exporter still has the trace and span IDs that map to the original request, but the logged header is blank on retry.

dan: is the retry code doing req = new Request(...) or cloning headers? some libs drop headers intentionally to avoid re-sending sensitive ones.

priya: i instrumented middleware order. sequence is: auth -> redact -> retry-builder -> otel-propagator -> logger. so on a retry we never run the propagator early enough to repopulate headers before the wire send. parity issue vs go which does auth -> otel-propagator -> retry-builder -> redact -> logger.

zoe: ah that explains it. so node's redact runs before the propagator on retry construction and strips x-request-id.

dan: two possible fixes: (A) reorder middleware so propagator always runs before any destructive redaction, or (B) capture req-id in a non-exported context/span attribute at first sight and have retry-builder prefer the context value when reconstructing the retry.

priya: i prefer B as a minimally-invasive change for rollouts. we can set span.setAttribute('rw.req_id', rid) on first parse and let logger/rehydrator read that. redaction remains eager for headers but internal context preserves the id.

zoe: ran a quick PoC: on first incoming request we set ctx = ctx.withValue(reqIdKey, rid) and span.setAttribute('rw.req_id', rid). retry-builder then does rid = ctx.Value(reqIdKey) || headers['x-request-id'] before sending. that keeps logs consistent across retries. pushed branch: https://git.internal/samples/pull/7

priya: two cautions: (1) if customers opt-out of exporting identifiers to traces we must honor that—add RW_EXPORT_REQID=false to prevent span attribute export, (2) ensure we don't leak it into stdout logs when RW_REDACT_MODE=aggressive; logging emission should still redact based on policy. the ctx should be internal-only until emission, and emission respects redact policy.

dan: agree. also add a small integration that forces aggressive redact and asserts that the internal ctx still contains req id while emitted headers are redacted. we should also normalize header case when reading.

replay-bot: created replay for the sample run so others can inspect: https://replay.internal/trace/1863456789

infra-bot: added CI job sample-e2e matrix with RW_REDACT_MODE={aggressive,deferred} and RW_EXPORT_REQID={true,false} (queued)

zoe: action items:
- priya to open a PR to add ctx-based preservation + RW_EXPORT_REQID guard (owner: priya)
- dan to add integration test to CI matrix and header normalization helper (owner: dan)
- zoe to update onboarding docs with a troubleshooting section about "missing req-id on retries" (owner: zoe)

priya: i'll land the PoC today and add tests. aiming to keep middleware ordering change for a follow-up since that may have broader effects.

zoe: thanks all! also adding a tiny note to sample-app README about toggling RW_REDACT_MODE locally to make debugging easier :thumbsup:
